business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Smart Utility Meters and Remote Telemetry Sensors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national civil law system with a distinct administrative law branch; Napoleonic Code tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed at Beijing on 30 May 1984; entered into force in 1985; still active and applicable where the ultimate beneficial owner is a Chinese resident)
France-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 30 May 1984; as amended by the 2013 Protocol; active and applicable to French-source dividend, interest and royalty flows to China)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49-55 (freedom of establishment; applicable to France as an EU member state and to EU-resident shareholders)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-49-1 and R. 561-1 to R. 561-59-1 (AML/CFT obligations, customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification and reporting to Tracfin); CMF Articles L. 561-45 to L. 561-47 and R. 561-45 to R. 561-47 (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE, maintained within the Registre du commerce et des sociétés); Code de commerce, Articles L. 123-1 to L. 123-12 and R. 123-10 to R. 123-97 (company registration and RBE integration); Décret n° 2020-1548 du 9 décembre 2020 (RBE filing procedures); Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020 as amended (transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843); CMF Articles L. 562-1 et seq. and R. 562-1 et seq. (asset freezing, financial sanctions and ministerial orders).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card for every shareholder, statutory director (Président/Directeur Général) and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorised administrative authority in the country of issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961; where the country of issue is not party to the Convention, Consular Legalization at the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and constitutive instruments (memorandum and articles of association) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the corporate shareholder's country of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the country of formation; for non-Hague countries, legalization visa from the French Consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) for the French SAS, containing the full ownership chain and voting rights schedule, signed by the proposed Président
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed SAS Président / legal representative; the declaration may be integrated in the articles or annexed to the RBE filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature in the articles before a French notary where notarized articles are used; if executed abroad before a foreign notary, the notarial certificate must bear a Hague Apostille or be legalized by the French Consulate as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney (pouvoir spécial) authorizing the local incorporation agent or avocat to execute and file the constitutive formalities and the RCS application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each shareholder or duly authorised representative of a corporate shareholder, executed before a notary public in the jurisdiction of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the notary / competent authority; for non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization at the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent original bank statement or banker's letter evidencing funding capacity for the SAS share capital and source of funds for the first AML/CFT source-of-funds verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy of the bank letter/statement, with Hague Apostille or consular legalization when issued from a foreign state; a banker's confirmation from a French bank is accepted without apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, legal representative, signatory and any person exercising control against: (i) the French PEP definition and list under CMF Article L. 561-10-2; (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list administered by the European Commission and enforced by the Direction générale du Trésor; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated lists, including the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions list; (iv) French national asset-freezing orders under CMF Articles L. 562-1 et seq.; and (v) the US OFAC SDN list where USD-denominated wire transfers or Swift clearing are contemplated. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory upon any PEP, negative-media or high-risk country trigger, and any positive hit requires immediate escalation and, where required, reporting to Tracfin under CMF Article L. 561-15.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); official registry search through INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) and Infogreffe (Registre du commerce et des sociétés - RCS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may be in a foreign language but must be recorded in Latin script. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, etc.) must be transliterated phonetically into French-recognized Latin characters. The name must not be contrary to public order or morality, must not mislead as to legal form, and must include the 'SAS' suffix. The French registry does not accept graphic characters, logos, or symbols; accents and French punctuation are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal name-reservation register for corporate names; the 30-day period is the conventional validity of a pre-filing RCS/INPI negative search certificate. If the guichet unique or the greffe rejects the requested name because it is identical to or confusingly similar to an existing RCS registration, the applicant may (1) refile immediately with a modified distinctive name or suffix, or (2) challenge the refusal by applying to the Président du Tribunal de commerce in summary proceedings within fifteen days from notification, under Code de commerce Articles L. 123-5 and R. 123-97. Where refusal is based on third-party trademark rights, an INPI trademark clearance opinion and civil action for annulment or coexistence are advised.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible solely for the legal registered office through a regulated domiciliation service under Code de commerce Articles L. 123-11-2 and R. 123-167. However, for a smart electricity meter manufacturing company (ISIC 2651), a virtual office is not sufficient commercial substance. France requires physical operational premises for production, calibration, quality control, or at least a bonded storage and warranty service location to support import customs compliance, EU Directive 2014/32/EU (MID) conformity, and the siège de direction effective test for corporate tax residence under Code général des impôts Article 209.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by French tax authorities (DGFiP), customs, URSSAF and/or the greffe within the first 24 months after incorporation, given the manufacturing nature of the activity and the EU metering-directive conformity obligations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via Guichet unique / Infogreffe

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the incorporation file and RCS registration of the SAS through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, including the greffe registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (via Infogreffe)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal announcements newspaper (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cap and prevailing market tariff per line

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation for the first year (administrative virtual office at a regulated domiciliation provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regulated domiciliation service provider under Code de commerce R.123-167
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a 12-month domiciliation contract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn English-to-French translation and certification of all statutory documents (articles, UBO declaration, powers of attorney, corporate shareholder good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French sworn translator (traducteur assermenté, Cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per word/page with mandatory sworn certification certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille or consular legalization bundle for foreign shareholder, UBO identity and power-of-attorney documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries and competent foreign authorities in the respective shareholding jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing foreign notarial and consular tariff, passed through at cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French counsel pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting of the English/French law SAS statuts, drafting of the UBO declaration and legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (Avocat, Barreau de Paris)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee / hourly legal fee benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML compliance work: PEP, OFAC, UN/EU sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification and AML risk memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance provider / French law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory consultation for EU Directive 2014/32/EU (MID) conformity path for smart electricity meters and CE-marking prerequisite
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: EU notified body or industry technical consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for preliminary conformity gap analysis and quotation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII — Articles L.227-1 to L.227-24 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), Articles L.210-2 and L.210-6 (registration and legal personality), Articles L.225-12 and L.225-13 (share capital payment rules applicable through L.227-2); Book I, Title II, Chapter III (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, Articles L.123-1 et seq.); Décret n°2007-431 of 25 March 2007; M0 / Cerfa n°14793#03 administrative form.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; all incorporation filings are submitted electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which routes the dossier to the competent Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'une société (M0 form — Cerfa n°14793#03), filed as a fully dematerialized creation dossier via the Guichet Unique national single-window portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS (capital freely fixed in the articles); capital must be fully subscribed and at least 50% of in-cash contributions (numéraire) must be paid up at incorporation and deposited into a blocked escrow account with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the balance must be paid within five years; in-kind contributions are fully paid up and must be valued in the statutory auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Sole Shareholder subscribes in full the share capital of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, paid up to at least 50% into a blocked escrow account per Article L.227-2 of the Commercial Code; RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at ______, France, within the jurisdiction of the Commercial Court; RESOLVED, that ______ is appointed Président, vested with full powers to act within the corporate purpose and to represent the Company; RESOLVED, that the Président shall complete the M0 filing via the Guichet Unique, publish the legal notice, obtain the K-bis, open bank accounts, and discharge all declarations. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation drafting and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Drafting by licensed legal counsel or a French notaire (notaire public) where in-kind or real-property contributions are made; the statuts are signed by all shareholders before the M0 filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French, defining the corporate name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose (manufacture and sale of smart electricity meters, telemetry sensors and IoT grid hardware), duration, rules for the Président's powers, and share transfer restrictions. Verify name availability and trademark conflicts through the INPI online databases. Have each shareholder and the future Président sign every page and the last page of the statuts. If foreign shareholders or foreign corporate shareholders participate, obtain apostilled identity, corporate extract and address proof, each with French certified translation. If in-kind contributions are made, obtain the statutory auditor's valuation report before execution.
required_dossiers: Draft of the Articles of Association (Statuts) in the French language
Identity document and proof of residential or business address of each shareholder and of the future Président
For legal entity shareholders: certificate of registration (K-bis or equivalent) and identity documents of the legal representative
Apostilled and translated documents for non-French shareholders and officers (Hague Apostille Convention)
Statutory auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) for any in-kind contribution
Declaration of non-conviction of the Président (attestation de non-condamnation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any deficiency in the statuts (identity errors, defective signatures, missing mandatory clauses) is cured by executing a deed of rectification (acte rectificatif) signed by the same parties and attaching it to the original statuts before the M0 filing; if the defect is found after filing, the company files an additional deed and requests registry correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital into a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) chosen by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the signature of the statuts, open a capital deposit account in the name of the 'société en formation'. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions; at least 50% of in-cash contributions must be paid up prior to incorporation. The depositary institution issues the mandatory 'attestation de dépôt des fonds', certifying the amount and confirming that the funds are blocked and cannot be drawn until the company is registered in the RCS. Upon issuance of the K-bis, the Président or a specifically authorized representative releases the funds into the corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft Articles of Association (Statuts) including the company name and capital amount
Identity documents and KYC/AML information of the depositor(s)
Source-of-funds evidence where requested by the bank under anti-money-laundering rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or rejects the deposit due to incomplete KYC/AML documentation, provide the requested source-of-funds declarations, bank references, and beneficial-ownership information to the institution; if the attestation is lost or defective, the depositary issues a replacement or rectified attestation before the M0 filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcement journal (JAL) published in the judicial district (département) where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the 'avis de constitution' containing the corporate form (SAS), company name, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, identity of the Président, and the court registry jurisdiction. Submit the notice to the chosen JAL with the capital deposit attestation. The JAL issues the 'attestation de parution' confirming the publication date, which is an annex to the M0 dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice (avis de constitution) duly drafted
Attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the depositary bank or CDC
Power of attorney where a founder is represented by another person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains errors, publish a corrective notice (avis rectificatif) and obtain a fresh attestation of publication; if the journal rejects the publication for lack of capital attestation, complete the prior capital deposit step and resubmit the notice to the same or another approved JAL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the M0 creation dossier via the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the dossier is transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the user account and open the 'création d'entreprise' application on the Guichet Unique platform. Complete all mandatory data fields of the M0 declaration, attach the scanned annexes, validate the tax and social regime selections, pay the registry and associated taxes online, and sign the electronic declaration. The platform performs formal completeness checks and transmits the dossier to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for legal verification and registration.
required_dossiers: M0 creation declaration (Cerfa n°14793#03) completed online
Executed copy of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds from the depositary institution
Attestation de parution from the legal gazette (JAL)
Apostilled identity and address proofs of shareholders and the Président, with French translations where applicable
Declaration of non-conviction of the Président
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contributions (if applicable)
Power of attorney and identity proof of the legalization agent if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the Greffe issues a deficiency notice (demande de complément), the applicant must complete or rectify the dossier within 15 days through the online platform; if the deadline is missed the application is abandoned and a new M0 filing must be made; substantive refusals may be challenged before the registry monitoring judge (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) or by correcting the underlying defects and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the registered office jurisdiction; supervision by the juge commis à la surveillance du registre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the verified dossier from the Guichet Unique, the registrar reviews legal compliance, orders the registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, and issues the company's K-bis extract. The company thereby acquires legal personality and is assigned its SIREN, SIRET, and the APE/NAF code (expected 2651B — manufacture of measuring and control instruments) and is automatically notified to INSEE, URSSAF and the DGFiP.
required_dossiers: None — the K-bis extract is generated by the registry from the already accepted M0 dossier; no further documents are required from the company at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration order contains errors in the company name, address, capital or officer details, file a rectification request with the Greffe; if registration is refused, examine the deficiency notice, remedy the stated irregularities, and either re-file the M0 or challenge the decision before the tribunal judiciaire within the applicable time limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration formalities: governance activation, bank account, insurance and establishment opening declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP (tax registration confirmation), DREETS (labour inspection and opening declaration), professional liability insurers, and the municipal planning/occupancy authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the K-bis is obtained, convene the first general meeting or founder's decision: ratify the appointment of the Président, approve the opening of a corporate bank account, adopt any internal rules (règlement intérieur), and authorize the subscription of general civil liability, product liability, and environmental liability insurance. Deposit the released share capital into the operative bank account. File the 'déclaration d'ouverture d'établissement' with the URSSAF/DREETS, confirm the company's tax and social regime, and initiate the industrial licensing and environmental authorization steps required for the manufacturing facility.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Articles of Association (Statuts)
Identity document of the Président
Corporate bank account opening evidence
Lease or registered office domiciliation agreement
Establishment opening declaration to URSSAF/DREETS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment opening declaration is late or incomplete, submit the declaration as soon as possible and pay any pro-rated late fees; if the bank account opening is queried, supplement KYC documents and the K-bis extract; if mandatory governance resolutions are missing, cure by a retrospective founder's decision confirming the acts performed on behalf of the company in formation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREETS (Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités) as the labour and ICPE inspection authority; Préfecture for the prefectoral prescriptions order; DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) as the environmental assessment authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permit: ICPE operating declaration or registration — 'Récépissé de déclaration ICPE' or 'Arrêté préfectoral d'enregistrement' for the classified installation (electronic assembly, component warehousing and testing of smart meters); where applicable, the 'Déclaration d'ouverture d'établissement industriel' under the Labour Code; supplementary 'Certificat de conformité électrique' of the facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) — service in charge of environmental impact assessment and classified installations; in liaison with the Préfecture and DREETS.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Registration / Declaration tier (ICPE regime, not full authorization): the activity of assembling and testing smart electricity meters does not, in a standard urban industrial zone, trigger a full EIA Report; a simplified environmental impact assessment (notice d'incidence / étude d'incidence) is submitted with the ICPE declaration or registration file; full EIA Report obligation applies only where the project exceeds the EU EIA Directive Annex II thresholds or is located in a protected or sensitive zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the ICPE general prescriptions (ministerial orders, including the arrêté of 2 February 1998) and municipal sanitation regulations: wastewater pH 5.5–9.5; total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L; BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L; COD ≤ 125 mg/L; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) ≤ 20 mg/Nm³ for coating and cleaning operations; compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions; product compliance with RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU; company registration as producer of electrical and electronic equipment under WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU via ADEME; waste tracking with appropriate registers for hazardous electronic waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and occupational clearance: mandatory inspection and certification by the departmental fire and rescue service (SDIS) with an approved fire safety visit; CONSUEL electrical conformity certificate for the production unit; structural load inspection confirming the building's suitability for electronic assembly, battery storage, and testing benches; workplace health and safety clearance by the labour inspectorate (DREETS) under Labour Code Books IV and V covering emergency exits, first aid, ventilation, personal protective equipment, and the single health and safety risk assessment document (DUERP); the company must maintain on-site the mandatory safety registers and post the employee safety instructions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Tax administration portal: impots.gouv.fr. Business formation and registration filings are generally submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing produces the legal registration and SIREN identifier, with an establishment-level SIRET identifier where applicable. The company requests or confirms its intra-Community VAT identification number through the competent SIE or the applicable online DGFiP procedure. A foreign entity carrying out taxable transactions in France must identify its French VAT obligations, appoint a French tax representative where legally required for a non-EU entity, submit the required registration documentation, and obtain a French VAT number before the relevant taxable transactions or within the applicable statutory period. Typical supporting documents include constitutional documents, foreign tax-registration evidence, proof of business activity, details of the French establishment or taxable operations, identity and authority documents for the representative, and banking information. The French VAT number generally uses the format FR followed by a two-character validation key and the entity's SIREN number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. An eligible SAS may elect corporate income tax treatment to be replaced temporarily by income tax treatment for up to five financial years, subject to statutory conditions concerning ownership, management, employee headcount, turnover or balance-sheet limits, business activity, and shareholder consent. The election must be filed within the applicable deadline with the competent tax authority and is generally irrevocable after the permitted period. France has no general United States-style check-the-box election for SAS entities. Separate elections may apply for VAT regimes, including the franchise in basis, the simplified regime, or the normal regime, subject to statutory eligibility and turnover conditions. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT for goods entering France from outside the European Union.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, VAT applies based on the nature and location of taxable transactions. The principal franchise-in-basis thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods, sales for consumption on premises, and accommodation activities, and EUR 37,500 for services and non-commercial activities, subject to statutory increased thresholds and annual legislative adjustments. Exceeding the applicable threshold or voluntarily opting into VAT generally triggers VAT collection and filing obligations. Imports, intra-Community acquisitions, and certain cross-border transactions may create VAT obligations independently of domestic turnover thresholds. A smart-meter manufacturer ordinarily falls within the goods threshold, but installation, maintenance, software, and other services must be analyzed separately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction reporting in phases. All French-established businesses must be capable of receiving compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuance obligations apply from 1 September 2026 to large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises, subject to the statutory definitions and any official transition measures. Invoices must generally pass through an approved private platform or the public invoicing platform architecture designated under French rules. France does not generally require real-time fiscal clearance of every domestic B2B invoice. Transaction data and, where applicable, payment data for transactions outside the domestic e-invoicing perimeter must be reported electronically under the e-reporting regime. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Electronic records must preserve invoice integrity, authenticity, readability, auditability, and required VAT information.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the exporter can substantiate the export and satisfy the statutory conditions. Required evidence normally includes the customs export declaration, an exit result or equivalent customs confirmation, and commercial and transport records linking the goods to the transaction. Supplies to customers in another EU Member State are generally treated as intra-Community supplies rather than third-country exports and require valid customer VAT identification, transport evidence, and appropriate recapitulative reporting. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under place-of-supply rules, rather than technically zero-rated, subject to exceptions for services connected with French real estate, events, transport, and other special categories. Refund or deduction claims require valid purchase invoices, proper accounting, and a direct connection with taxable transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration submitted through the applicable electronic customs system
Master Reference Number (MRN) and customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof of exit from the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and transaction reference
Packing list and product description, including serial numbers or model references where relevant
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other transport document
Transport, delivery, freight-forwarder, and logistics records linking the goods to the export declaration
Proof of payment or contractual and accounting records supporting the transaction where requested by the tax authority
Export sales ledger and VAT return records showing the exempt export with right of deduction

Inward remittance evidence only where relevant to a contractual, banking, financing, or audit requirement; France has no general VAT rule requiring an inward remittance certificate for export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds and no general requirement to obtain an inward remittance certificate as a condition of VAT exemption. The exporter must retain reliable evidence that the goods left the European Union and that the transaction was correctly reported. If zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the DGFiP may assess output VAT retroactively, deny or recover related input-VAT deductions or refunds, charge late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and impose tax penalties commonly ranging from 10% for specified late or corrective situations to 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, depending on the facts and applicable provision. Customs infringements may generate separate duties, VAT, fines, seizure, or other customs measures. Intentional tax fraud may also create criminal exposure, including imprisonment and substantial fines, subject to the applicable aggravated-fraud rules. The taxpayer bears the burden of preserving export and transport evidence and must correct unsupported claims through amended VAT returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and Direction Generale du Tresor (French Treasury) acting as the foreign exchange regulatory authority under the French Monetary and Financial Code
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions in France. No exchange control restrictions are imposed on trade or investment flows; however, cross-border fund movements must comply with EU customs declarations, economic sanctions, and balance-of-payments reporting obligations. Dividend distributions and shareholder current-account repayments are freely permitted provided corporate formalities are satisfied, distributable reserves are available, and the relevant tax clearance and anti-avoidance declarations are current.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency onshore or offshore in designated FX deposit accounts. All export-related fund flows must nonetheless be declared under EU customs rules and, for resident entities, reportable monetary statistics must be filed with the Banque de France for cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 per direct investment transaction or EUR 50,000 in capital movements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility of using offshore digital EMI providers is Medium, subject to strict operational limits. An EMI incorporated within the EEA holding an e-money licence may passport into France and provide ancillary payment accounts; however, it cannot replace a tier-1 French commercial bank for treasury functions requiring trade finance, statutorily compliant escrow arrangements, or local LC settlement. Legal constraints include the AMF/BAC-FIN AML reporting framework, PSD2 conduct rules, and the prohibition on using an offshore account without a correspondent banking relationship where settlement is presented in France. Such EMI accounts are therefore viable only for travel/operational expenses, name-discrepant small-value payments, and temporary FX liquidity, not for capital-injection escrow or large-scale LC disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For tier-1 French banks, physical presence of the corporate legal representative or a duly authorised director with valid power of attorney at the initial KYC interview is generally preferred and often mandatory for non-resident entities. Remote onboarding using video identification and electronic signature is permitted at some institutions, but will typically be conditioned on completing a live video interview, presenting notarised and apostilled corporate sign-off, and supplying bank references. Foreign directors may be required to attend in person if the bank's internal AML risk profile mandates enhanced due diligence. In all cases, a remote interview combined with a local in-person appearance by the company's French executive agent or registered legal counsel is a proven workable solution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identified as a non-resident high-net-worth individual without clear source of wealth or commercial background for manufacturing activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; bank statements demonstrating historical asset accumulation; signed source-of-wealth letter; tax residence certificate; French UBO declaration filed with the Commercial Registry; detailed business plan; smart-meter sector resume of the shareholders; forecast balance sheet and profit and loss projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company has minimal French substance, no local employees, and relies exclusively on outsourced management and board members
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed French office lease agreement in the company's name with rent receipts; French social security filings for all local personnel; full-service administration contract with a registered French accountant; proof of physical inventory or third-party logistics warehousing in France; minutes of the board meeting resolving substance measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border payment flow includes high-value invoices to non-EU counterparties or to entities in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the export control and sanctions policy; list of target jurisdictions cleared by external counsel; ICC/ATLAS export-compliant documentation; transaction-level statistical profile; proof of compliance with EU Regulation 2018/1672 on monetary controls; evidence of final-buyer certification for grid infrastructure goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with a broad digital-commerce purpose perceived as a potential shell or pass-through entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founding statutes and company K-bis; executed smart-meter supply agreement and distributor contract; CE, MID metrology and telecom certifications; production background and factory-inspection report for the assembled product; operating bank statements showing positive cash balance and actual trade payables/receivables.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for shareholder capital injection into an SAS: settle EUR via SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT MT103; classify the transaction under CMF as 'investissement direct' and use purpose code E (foreign direct investment) or PF; complete the declaration de transfert de fonds (DTF) to Direction Generale des Douanes et Droits Indirects and the Banque de France for equity inflows exceeding EUR 50,000; keep board minutes evidencing capital increase and issue unissued shares concurrently; do not commingle operational receipts with capital injection. For USD inbound payments, pre-clear via a US correspondent bank by providing the ultimate beneficiary's IBAN, SWIFT BIC and the exact purpose wording 'Capital contribution to a French SAS'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 with cover payment for regular supplier disbursements under open-account trading; (2) irrevocable, confirmed commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 and eUCP 2.0 for project-milestone payments to international counterparties; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EUR supplier payments across EEA; (4) SWIFT gpi tracker overlay for real-time cross-border payment transparency. All outbound remittances must carry a mandatory UETR, presend the correct purpose code mapped to the French PEEC/BNC or OECD service classification, and be supported by underlying contract, invoice, and customs documents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR; administrative strike-off possible after formal notice and non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual deadline; mandatory update upon any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR; potential director liability and administrative sanctions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (révision légale) if company exceeds two of: turnover > 800,000 EUR, balance sheet total > 400,000 EUR, or employees > 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update and filing of Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (DBE) with tax authorities
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors' Decisions (Registre des décisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for SMEs on first €42,500 of taxable profit; R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible expenses); accelerated depreciation for qualifying assets; investment tax credit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200A - Déclaration de résultat (corporate income tax return) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the fiscal year (e.g., May 15 for calendar year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of taxable profit after all adjustments and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income; attach relevant DTA forms if claiming treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions, exemptions, and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents limited to French-source items; submit TRC for reduced rates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €200, maximum 10% of tax due)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid to non-resident corporate recipients (EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and most DTAs)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Treaty Relief Certificate) to withholding agent including beneficial ownership certificate and specific DTA article reference
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under most treaties; Interest: 0% under most treaties (reduced from statutory 25%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group turnover triggers mandatory local file and master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities engaged in certain activities including IP holding, finance, and administration; manufacturing entities must demonstrate adequate substance for tax residency claims

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations to tax authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to 80% of evaded tax; civil restitution obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, imprisonment, and disqualification from corporate management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain TP documentation or use of aggressive TP positions lacking economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to €100,000 or 5% of turnover; potential recharacterization of intra-group transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal joint and several liability for tax debts in case of fraudulent conduct or misrepresentation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Comply with Economic Substance Requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without adequate local substance for claimed tax benefits or residency purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax benefits, back taxes, penalties up to €10,000 per day of non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for misrepresentation, possible fines and imprisonment for willful violations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct due diligence or report suspicious transactions in cross-border dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of turnover; criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, and potential jail time for willful non-compliance
